# setuptools and pyproject.toml

The packaging layer that turns twelve lab scripts into one installable project in
[[python-programming-laboratories]]. This is the mechanism behind
[[extract-the-shared-core]] — without it, "shared core" would just mean a file everyone copies.

## src-layout

The package lives at `src/weblog/`, not `weblog/` at the repo root. The difference matters: with a
root-level package, `import weblog` in a test picks up the working directory copy whether or not the
install succeeded, so a broken package configuration passes tests locally and fails for everyone
else. Under src-layout the only importable `weblog` is the installed one.

`pyproject.toml` sets `pythonpath` for [[pytest]] so the suite still resolves imports without an
editable install already in place.

## The extras split

```toml
dependencies = []
```

> "# Only the later laboratories need these; the core package has no dependencies."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/pyproject.toml, 2026-07-25

The core — parsing, reading, stats, config, CLI — is stdlib only, using [[argparse]] rather than
[[click]] for exactly this reason. Everything else goes into optional extras:

- **`labs`** — [[click]], openpyxl, [[factory-boy-and-faker]], requests, [[beautifulsoup]],
  [[matplotlib]], [[pillow]], python-docx.
- **`dev`** — `pytest`, `pytest-cov`.

Installing the core installs nothing else, which is [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] expressed as
metadata rather than as a claim.

  never mentioned in the README. `confidence: low` on any claim that it was used.

## The split has a hole

The `dev` extra omits `factory_boy` and `Faker`, which `tests/test_lab09_insults.py` imports — so the
README's documented quick start fails at collection in a clean virtualenv. Recorded in full on
[[factory-boy-and-faker]]. Declaring dependencies precisely is the whole value of this file, and this
is the one place it is wrong.
